domain_claim: MAX_TRIM_KEY_LEN and MAX_SNAPSHOT_KEY_LEN are pub(crate) const aliases that are compile-time equal to JOURNAL_KEY_BYTES == 17; the alias chain (const A = B; const B = 17) makes drift impossible.
notes: Compile-time invariant; verification is a single unit test asserting assert_eq!(MAX_TRIM_KEY_LEN, 17) and assert_eq!(MAX_SNAPSHOT_KEY_LEN, 17). No formal verifier needed because const alias equality is a static property of stable Rust. The cargo-check gate runs on every moon ci pass and would fail if any const diverged. Owner_state: planned (State 3 contract stage). Behavior_affecting: false because the constant change does not alter runtime behavior; the literal 17 and the named cap both gate the same set of keys.

domain_claim: latest_durable_snapshot_seq rejects any raw key whose key.len() != MAX_SNAPSHOT_KEY_LEN with Err(TrimError::IncompleteTrim { deleted_count: 0 }); the test pins both a 13-byte planted key (existing) and an overlong 24-byte planted key (new).
notes: Augmented test must plant a raw key under PREFIX_RUN_SNAPSHOT whose length is strictly greater than 17 (e.g., 9 prefix+run bytes + 15 trailing bytes = 24 bytes) and assert the same Err(TrimError::IncompleteTrim { deleted_count: 0 }) the existing 13-byte test asserts. The integration test uses temp_journal() to spin up a real Fjall instance and insert the malformed row via journal.run_snapshot.insert(...). Behavior_affecting: true because the fix closes a P1 bug (Round 10 issue 7) where an overlong raw key would have been misread as a canonical snapshot.

domain_claim: trim_events_for_run rejects any raw key whose key.len() != MAX_TRIM_KEY_LEN with Err(TrimError::IncompleteTrim { deleted_count }); the test pins both a 9-byte planted key (existing) and an overlong 24-byte planted key (new).
notes: Augmented test must plant a raw key under PREFIX_RUN_EVENT whose length is strictly greater than 17 (e.g., 9 prefix+run bytes + 15 trailing bytes = 24 bytes) and assert Err(TrimError::IncompleteTrim { .. }). The integration test uses temp_journal() and ensures that a valid 17-byte event is also planted so the loop iterates past the first key. Behavior_affecting: true because the fix prevents the trim loop from silently truncating or skipping a corrupt row, which would cause wrong-event deletion.

domain_claim: count_trimmable_events (via trim_eligibility_diagnostic) rejects any raw key whose key.len() != MAX_TRIM_KEY_LEN with Err(JournalError::Trim(Box::new(TrimError::IncompleteTrim { deleted_count }))); the test pins both a 9-byte planted key (existing) and an overlong 24-byte planted key (new).
notes: Augmented test plants an overlong raw key under PREFIX_RUN_EVENT and asserts that trim_eligibility_diagnostic returns Err(JournalError::Trim(inner)) where inner is TrimError::IncompleteTrim. The test must follow the existing structural pattern at trimming/tests.rs:979-985 (unwrap the Box and assert the inner variant). Behavior_affecting: true because the diagnostic function feeds a planning UI; miscounting trimmable events because of a corrupt row would mislead the operator.
